1	# Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	
     5	URL: https://radar.cloudflare.com/year-in-review/2024
     6	
     7	The Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review provides a comprehensive view of Internet patterns and trends observed through Cloudflare's global network during 2024. The report covers traffic growth, popular services, technology adoption, connectivity disruptions, security threats, and email security trends. Data is derived from Cloudflare's position as a provider protecting and accelerating websites and applications for millions of customers worldwide.
     8	
     9	## Internet Traffic Growth and Popular Services
    10	
    11	Global Internet traffic grew by 17% in 2024, continuing the upward trend driven by increasing reliance on the Internet for communication, commerce, entertainment, and transportation. The trend line starts mid-January to normalize for post-holiday activity.
    12	
    13	Google maintained its position as the most popular Internet service overall, topping the rankings for the second consecutive year. Generative AI continued its rapid rise throughout 2024, while the Metaverse receded into the background. The ranking methodology is based on aggregate data from Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver.
    14	
    15	| Rank | Service   |
    16	|------|-----------|
    17	| #1   | Google    |
    18	| #2   | Facebook  |
    19	| #3   | Apple     |
    20	| #4   | TikTok    |
    21	| #5   | AWS       |
    22	| #6   | Microsoft |
    23	| #7   | Instagram |
    24	| #8   | YouTube   |
    25	| #9   | Amazon    |
    26	| #10  | WhatsApp  |
    27	
    28	![Top 10 most popular Internet services worldwide](./assets/top-10-internet-services.jpg)
    29	
    30	SpaceX Starlink traffic saw dramatic 3.3x growth during 2024, continuing to bring satellite Internet connectivity to previously underserved locations. Starlink is not yet available globally; the trend line is scaled relative to peak observed request volume.
    31	
    32	![Normalized Starlink traffic worldwide showing 3.3x growth in 2024](./assets/starlink-traffic-growth-2024.jpg)
    33	
    34	## Technology Adoption and Usage Patterns
    35	
    36	Several key adoption metrics emerged from the 2024 data:
    37	
    38	- **Mobile OS**: 33% of traffic came from iOS devices. Apple iOS and Google Android remain the dominant mobile operating systems, with peak Android traffic share exceeding 95% in some regions and peak iOS reaching around 66%.
    39	- **HTTP/3**: 21% of traffic uses HTTP/3, the most recent version of the protocol that runs on top of QUIC, providing faster connections, packet-loss mitigation, and encryption by default.
    40	- **Search Engines**: Google dominates with 89% of search engine referral traffic, followed by Yandex (3.1%), Baidu (2.7%), Bing (2.6%), DuckDuckGo (0.95%), and other engines (2.2%).
    41	- **Browsers**: Chrome remains the most popular browser globally.
    42	- **API Client Languages**: Go is the most popular API client language with approximately 12% of automated API requests, followed by Node.js, Python (9.6%), Java (7.4%), and .NET (3.6%).
    43	
    44	Post-quantum encryption saw a dramatic surge in adoption during 2024. Starting at around 2% of TLS 1.3 traffic in early 2024, adoption jumped sharply following Google Chrome 124 enabling post-quantum key agreement by default on April 17, rapidly climbing to approximately 12-13%. Mozilla Firefox has also started rolling out post-quantum by default, and Apple Safari began initial testing.
    45	
    46	![Post-quantum encrypted traffic worldwide showing rapid adoption after Chrome 124 release](./assets/post-quantum-encryption-adoption.jpg)
    47	
    48	## Internet Connectivity and Disruptions
    49	
    50	Cloudflare observed 225 major Internet disruptions globally in 2024. These outages result from a variety of causes, and the Cloudflare Radar Outage Center tracks their scope and duration using Cloudflare traffic data.
    51	
    52	The leading causes of Internet disruptions were:
    53	
    54	| Cause                | Count |
    55	|----------------------|-------|
    56	| Government Directed  | 116+  |
    57	| Cable Cut            | 41    |
    58	| Unknown              | 16    |
    59	| Power Outage         | 16    |
    60	| Technical Problem    | 9     |
    61	| Military Action      | 9     |
    62	| Weather              | 8     |
    63	| Maintenance          | 4     |
    64	| Cyber Attack         | 4     |
    65	| Natural Disaster     | 1     |
    66	| Fire                 | 1     |
    67	
    68	![Causes of major Internet disruptions observed in 2024](./assets/internet-disruption-causes.jpg)
    69	
    70	IPv6 adoption reached 28% of dual-stack traffic during 2024. Spain recorded the highest download speed among all countries measured.
    71	
    72	41% of global traffic came from mobile devices, reflecting the continued importance of mobile connectivity worldwide.
    73	
    74	## Security Landscape
    75	
    76	Cloudflare mitigated 6.5% of all traffic it processed, indicating the scale of ongoing threats. The Gambling and Games sector was the most attacked industry category. Notably, 68% of global bot traffic originated from just the top 10 countries.
    77	
    78	The Log4j vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228), first disclosed in December 2021, continues to be actively targeted by attackers more than two years later, underscoring the persistent nature of widely known vulnerabilities.
    79	
    80	RPKI (Resource Public Key Infrastructure) valid routes increased by 6.4%, an important step toward improved Internet routing security.
    81	
    82	## Email Security Threats
    83	
    84	Cloudflare's email security analysis revealed that 4.3% of emails processed were malicious. Among those malicious emails, 43% contained a deceptive link designed to trick recipients. The top-level domain .bar originated the largest share of malicious and spam email observed during the year.
    85	
    86	## Key Findings
    87	
    88	- Global Internet traffic grew 17% year-over-year, with Starlink traffic surging 3.3x as satellite connectivity expanded to underserved regions.
    89	- Post-quantum encryption adoption leapt from approximately 2% to 13% of TLS 1.3 traffic following Chrome 124's default enablement in April 2024.
    90	- Government-directed shutdowns remained the leading cause of the 225 major Internet disruptions observed, followed by cable cuts (41 incidents) and power outages (16).
    91	- Security threats remained pervasive: 6.5% of all traffic was mitigated, Gambling/Games was the most targeted sector, and Log4j exploitation persists years after disclosure.
    92	- Go surpassed other languages to become the most popular API client language, capturing roughly 12% of automated API traffic.

    51	
    52	# PPTX Manipulation Skill
    53	
    54	## Overview
    55	
    56	This skill enables programmatic creation, editing, and manipulation of Microsoft PowerPoint (.pptx) presentations using the **python-pptx** library. Create professional slides with text, shapes, images, charts, and tables without manual editing.
    57	
    58	## How to Use
    59	
    60	1. Describe the presentation you want to create or modify
    61	2. Provide content, data, or images to include
    62	3. I'll generate python-pptx code and execute it
    63	
    64	**Example prompts:**
    65	- "Create a 10-slide pitch deck from this outline"
    66	- "Add a chart to slide 3 with this data"
    67	- "Extract all text from this presentation"
    68	- "Generate slides from this markdown content"
    69	
    70	## Domain Knowledge
    71	
    72	### python-pptx Fundamentals
    73	
    74	```python
    75	from pptx import Presentation
    76	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
    77	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
    78	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
    79	
    80	# Create new presentation
    81	prs = Presentation()
    82	
    83	# Or open existing
    84	prs = Presentation('existing.pptx')
    85	```
    86	
    87	### Presentation Structure
    88	```
    89	Presentation
    90	├── slide_layouts (predefined layouts)
    91	├── slides (individual slides)
    92	│   ├── shapes (text, images, charts)
    93	│   │   ├── text_frame (paragraphs)
    94	│   │   └── table (rows, cells)
    95	│   └── placeholders (title, content)
    96	└── slide_masters (templates)
    97	```
    98	
    99	### Slide Layouts
   100	```python
   101	# Common layout indices (may vary by template)
   102	TITLE_SLIDE = 0
   103	TITLE_CONTENT = 1
   104	SECTION_HEADER = 2
   105	TWO_CONTENT = 3
   106	COMPARISON = 4
   107	TITLE_ONLY = 5
   108	BLANK = 6
   109	
   110	# Add slide with layout
   111	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[TITLE_CONTENT]
   112	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   113	```
   114	
   115	### Adding Content
   116	
   117	#### Title Slide
   118	```python
   119	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0]  # Title slide
   120	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   121	
   122	title = slide.shapes.title
   123	subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]
   124	
   125	title.text = "Quarterly Report"
   126	subtitle.text = "Q4 2024 Performance Review"
   127	```
   128	
   129	#### Text Content
   130	```python
   131	# Using placeholder
   132	body = slide.placeholders[1]
   133	tf = body.text_frame
   134	tf.text = "First bullet point"
   135	
   136	# Add more paragraphs
   137	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   138	p.text = "Second bullet point"
   139	p.level = 0
   140	
   141	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   142	p.text = "Sub-bullet"
   143	p.level = 1
   144	```
   145	
   146	#### Text Box
   147	```python
   148	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   149	
   150	left = Inches(1)
   151	top = Inches(2)
   152	width = Inches(4)
   153	height = Inches(1)
   154	
   155	txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
   156	tf = txBox.text_frame
   157	
   158	p = tf.paragraphs[0]
   159	p.text = "Custom text box"
   160	p.font.bold = True
   161	p.font.size = Pt(18)
   162	```
   163	
   164	#### Shapes
   165	```python
   166	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
   167	
   168	# Rectangle
   169	shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
   170	    MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
   171	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # left, top
   172	    Inches(3), Inches(1.5) # width, height
   173	)
   174	shape.text = "Rectangle with text"
   175	
   176	# Common shapes:
   177	# MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, ROUNDED_RECTANGLE
   178	# MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, CHEVRON, ARROW_RIGHT
   179	# MSO_SHAPE.CALLOUT_ROUNDED_RECTANGLE
   180	```
   181	
   182	#### Images
   183	```python
   184	# Add image
   185	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   186	    'image.png',
   187	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # position
   188	    width=Inches(4)        # auto height
   189	)
   190	
   191	# Or specify both dimensions
   192	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   193	    'logo.png',
   194	    Inches(8), Inches(0.5),
   195	    Inches(1.5), Inches(0.75)
   196	)
   197	```
   198	
   199	### Tables
   200	```python
   201	# Create table
   202	rows, cols = 4, 3
   203	left = Inches(1)
   204	top = Inches(2)
   205	width = Inches(8)
   206	height = Inches(2)
   207	
   208	table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, height).table
   209	
   210	# Set column widths
   211	table.columns[0].width = Inches(2)
   212	table.columns[1].width = Inches(3)
   213	table.columns[2].width = Inches(3)
   214	
   215	# Add headers
   216	headers = ['Product', 'Q3 Sales', 'Q4 Sales']
   217	for i, header in enumerate(headers):
   218	    cell = table.cell(0, i)
   219	    cell.text = header
   220	    cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
   221	
   222	# Add data
   223	data = [
   224	    ['Widget A', '$10,000', '$12,500'],
   225	    ['Widget B', '$8,000', '$9,200'],
   226	    ['Widget C', '$15,000', '$18,000'],
   227	]
   228	for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data, 1):
   229	    for col_idx, value in enumerate(row_data):
   230	        table.cell(row_idx, col_idx).text = value
   231	```
   232	
   233	### Charts
   234	```python
   235	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   236	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   237	
   238	# Chart data
   239	chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   240	chart_data.categories = ['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4']
   241	chart_data.add_series('Sales', (19.2, 21.4, 16.7, 23.8))
   242	chart_data.add_series('Expenses', (12.1, 15.3, 14.2, 18.1))
   243	
   244	# Add chart
   245	x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1), Inches(2), Inches(8), Inches(4)
   246	chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   247	    XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED,
   248	    x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
   249	).chart
   250	
   251	# Customize
   252	chart.has_legend = True
   253	chart.legend.include_in_layout = False
   254	```

   256	### Formatting
   257	
   258	#### Text Formatting
   259	```python
   260	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   261	
   262	run = p.runs[0]
   263	run.font.name = 'Arial'
   264	run.font.size = Pt(24)
   265	run.font.bold = True
   266	run.font.italic = True
   267	run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x66, 0xCC)
   268	```
   269	
   270	#### Shape Fill & Line
   271	```python
   272	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   273	
   274	shape.fill.solid()
   275	shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x80, 0x00)
   276	
   277	shape.line.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
   278	shape.line.width = Pt(2)
   279	```
   280	
   281	#### Paragraph Alignment
   282	```python
   283	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
   284	
   285	p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER  # LEFT, RIGHT, JUSTIFY
   286	```
   287	
   288	## Best Practices
   289	
   290	1. **Use Templates**: Start with a .pptx template for consistent branding
   291	2. **Layout First**: Plan slide structure before coding
   292	3. **Reuse Slide Masters**: Maintain consistency across presentations
   293	4. **Optimize Images**: Compress images before adding
   294	5. **Test Output**: Always verify generated presentations
   295	
   296	## Common Patterns
   297	
   298	### Slide Deck Generator
   299	```python
   300	def create_deck(title, slides_content):
   301	    prs = Presentation()
   302	    
   303	    # Title slide
   304	    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   305	    slide.shapes.title.text = title
   306	    
   307	    # Content slides
   308	    for slide_data in slides_content:
   309	        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   310	        slide.shapes.title.text = slide_data['title']
   311	        
   312	        body = slide.placeholders[1]
   313	        tf = body.text_frame
   314	        for i, point in enumerate(slide_data['points']):
   315	            if i == 0:
   316	                tf.text = point
   317	            else:
   318	                p = tf.add_paragraph()
   319	                p.text = point
   320	    
   321	    return prs
   322	```
   323	
   324	### Data-Driven Charts
   325	```python
   326	def add_bar_chart(slide, title, categories, values):
   327	    from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   328	    from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   329	    
   330	    chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   331	    chart_data.categories = categories
   332	    chart_data.add_series('Values', values)
   333	    
   334	    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   335	        XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED,
   336	        Inches(1), Inches(2),
   337	        Inches(8), Inches(4),
   338	        chart_data
   339	    ).chart
   340	    
   341	    chart.chart_title.text_frame.text = title
   342	    return chart
   343	```

   345	## Examples
   346

   389	slide.shapes.add_chart(

   399	### Example 2: Report with Data Table

   437

# ── Helpers ──
def set_slide_bg(slide, color):
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=Pt(14),
                font_color=WHITE, bold=False, italic=False, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                font_name="Segoe UI"):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.alignment = align
    run = p.runs[0]
    run.font.size = font_size
    run.font.color.rgb = font_color
    run.font.bold = bold
    run.font.italic = italic
    run.font.name = font_name
    return txBox

def add_bullet_text(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets,
                    font_size=Pt(16), font_color=WHITE, font_name="Segoe UI"):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, bullet in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = bullet
        p.level = 0
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
        p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
        run = p.runs[0]
        run.font.size = font_size
        run.font.color.rgb = font_color
        run.font.name = font_name
    return txBox

def add_accent_bar(slide, left, top, width, height, color=ACCENT_ORANGE):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape

    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    if line_color:
        shape.line.color.rgb = line_color
        shape.line.width = Pt(1)
    else:
        shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape

    ("05", "Evolving Developer Ecosystem",
     "Go surpassed other languages to become the most popular API client language, capturing roughly 12% of automated API traffic.",
     ACCENT_BLUE),
]

card_w = Inches(12.133)
card_h = Inches(1.05)
start_y = Inches(1.2)
for i, (num, title, body, color) in enumerate(takeaways):
    y = start_y + i * (card_h + Inches(0.15))
    add_rounded_rect(slide, Inches(0.6), y, card_w, card_h, DARK_BLUE)
    # Number
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.75), y + Inches(0.18), Inches(0.6), Inches(0.6),
                num, font_size=Pt(22), bold=True, font_color=color)
    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(1.5), y + Inches(0.12), Inches(3.0), Inches(0.4),
                title, font_size=Pt(15), bold=True, font_color=WHITE)
    # Body
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(1.5), y + Inches(0.45), Inches(11.0), Inches(0.5),
                body, font_size=Pt(12), font_color=MED_GRAY)

# Footer
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.7), Inches(12.133), Inches(0.3),
            "Source: Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review  |  radar.cloudflare.com/year-in-review/2024",
            font_size=Pt(11), align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER, font_color=DARK_GRAY)

# ── Save ──
prs.save(OUTPUT_PATH)
print(f"Saved presentation to {OUTPUT_PATH}")
